What is PHP and why did it take government websites offline?
item.description:
CYBERSECURITY-PHP/BUGS

Government websites across Europe went dark on Wednesday as operators raced to patch two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, one of the most widely used programming languages on the web.

The developers of PHP said on Wednesday they would release patches for two critical vulnerabilities, and EU cybersecurity officials warned organisations unable to apply the fixes to take affected websites offline. Here is what you need to know:

Websites shut down worldwide amid fears of cyberattacks: How prepared is Bangladesh?

What is PHP?

PHP is a programming language that runs websites. It works behind the scenes. When a user loads a page, the server running PHP assembles the content and sends the finished page to the browser.

It is free, open source and maintained by volunteers. Site owners rarely interact with it directly.

PHP runs nearly 70 per cent of all websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs. It is the engine behind WordPress, the software that powers about 40 per cent of all websites such as blogs, small business pages, government portals, online shops and news sites.

What are the Risks of the Flaws?

The two vulnerabilities are rated 9.2 out of 10 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale, a standard industry scoring system. CERT-EU, the European Union's cybersecurity response team, said that rating signals unauthenticated remote code execution, meaning an attacker can run commands on a vulnerable server, over the internet, with no password or account.

PHP flaws: Bangladesh Bank, land services, six banks’ websites remain offline

A single flaw in PHP opens the same door on millions of servers at once. Whoever exploits the flaw controls the website. GoDaddy, a web hosting provider, said that could mean stolen data, defaced pages or full-system compromise. Cloudflare's chief technology officer said early attacks were emerging.

Most small websites are typically run by owners with no security staff, often on shared hosting where they do not manage the server and may not know who updates PHP. Wordfence, a security plugin for WordPress sites, warned that the usual automatic updates will not apply this fix. CERT-EU's guidance is to take affected sites offline rather than leave them exposed.

How was it Found?

Researchers at security firm Calif, working with OpenAI, reported the first flaw to PHP on 11 August after finding it with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, the company said. Wiz, a security firm owned by Alphabet's GOOGL.O Google, found the flaws independently and reported a second one on August 24, also using AI models.

Wiz said the findings "rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history." The underlying flaws had been present for decades, the firm said, but proving they were exploitable required a chain of steps "at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve."

US President Donald Trump's administration said it was "tracking and coordinating with federal agencies and leading SI labs to expedite the release of the fix," referring to Trump's preferred name for artificial intelligence. It framed the discovery as evidence that American "Super Intelligence" strengthens national security.

PHP flaws prompt millions of hacking attempts amid rush to patch vulnerabilities

item.title: Puja holidays: Tk 5m, 8 bhori of gold missing from home
item.description:
Sukhan Chowdhury (50) sold land in his village, with the dream of setting up a dyeing factory. The deal for purchasing the dyeing equipment was finalised.

He kept Tk 5 million from the land sale in a wardrobe of his house in Narsingdi and went to his village to celebrate Durga Puja. After returning from the Puja, he found everything ransacked. Tk 5 million meant for the factory and his wife’s eight bhori of gold jewelry had been stolen from the wardrobe.

The burglary took place in a flat on the second floor of the seven-story building owned by Naresh Chandra Saha in the Sebasangha area of Narsingdi city. Sukhan Chowdhury, along with his wife and children, has been living in this flat for five years. He works at Eva Dyeing in Shekherchar, Narsingdi Sadar upazila. His village home is in Guhiala village of Barhatta Upazila, Netrokona.

Yesterday, Friday night, Sukhan Chowdhury filed a written complaint at Narsingdi Model Police Station.

He told Prothom Alo, "I brought Tk 5 million home by selling village land to start a dyeing factory. The discussion to buy the dyeing equipment was finalised. My wife's jewelry was also there. While we were away from home, everything was stolen within the last six days. The thieves have stolen my lifelong dream of starting a dyeing factory."

Sukhon's wife, Purabi Pandit, said they locked the Narsingdi house and went to their village home last Sunday afternoon for Durga Puja. They returned to the Narsingdi house around 8 pm yesterday, Friday. Despite having the key, they couldn't open the flat's door. Even after breaking the lock, the door wouldn’t open, raising their suspicion. Going to the back of the house, they found the window grill cut.

With the help of locals, Sukhan entered through the grilled window. Once he opened the flat's door, everyone saw that the furniture and clothes were scattered around, and the wardrobe was broken. The eight tola of gold jewelry and Tk 5 million intended for the factory were missing.

MR Al Mamun, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Narsingdi Model Police Station, told Prothom Alo that they have received a written complaint about the burglary.

CCTV footage from the scene is being collected. The individuals involved will be identified and brought to justice swiftly.

item.title: Murder, robbery and extortion; police also attacked during operations
item.description:
Fishermen are losing their lives in pirate gunfire while out fishing. Boat workers are being beaten and hacked with machetes for refusing to pay extortion money. Cargo vessels are being looted, with fertiliser and other goods being stolen. Other crimes committed along river routes include kidnapping, robbery, drug smuggling and illegal sand extraction. Members of the River Police are also coming under attack while conducting operations to prevent these crimes.

Several senior River Police officials told Prothom Alo that fear intensifies along river routes as soon as night falls. Attacks and other criminal activities are taking place on various types of vessels, including passenger trawlers, fishing boats, cargo vessels and bulkheads.

According to the officials, criminals are increasingly choosing river routes because law enforcement surveillance is less extensive there than on land, despite the vast stretches of waterways that need to be monitored. As a result, river-related crime is on the rise.

The River Police divides the country’s waterways into 11 regions to maintain law and order and control crime. In these regions, a total of 2,085 cases were filed in 2024 involving murder, unnatural deaths, robbery, snatching, weapons, transportation of stolen goods, illegal sand extraction, kidnapping, extortion and drug-related offences. In 2025, the number of cases rose to 3,399—an increase of 1,314 in a single year.

From January to September this year, a further 505 cases were filed involving murder, robbery, kidnapping, piracy and unnatural deaths. Combining all categories of cases recorded in the previous two years with these five categories of cases filed during the first nine months of this year brings the total to 5,989.

Fisherman killed, vessels robbed

On the night of 1 February last year, a fisherman named Md. Hossain, 30, was killed by pirate gunfire while fishing in the Meghna River near East Ilisha union in Bhola Sadar upazila. Three other fishermen—Abbas, 32, Kanchan, 34, and Sohel, 29—were injured in the shooting. All four were residents of Baghar Hawla village in Bhola Sadar upazila.
The River Police said a group of river pirates attempted to rob the fishermen’s trawler that night. When the fishermen tried to resist, the pirates opened fire on them. The incident spread fear among fishermen in the area.

Shah Alam Mallick, general secretary of the Bangladesh Fishermen’s Federation, told Prothom Alo that robbers and river pirates attack fishing boats and passenger vessels along river routes bordering five districts.
The attacks generally take place after dusk in several areas: Haimechar in Chandpur; Lakshmichar and Kachikata in Shariatpur; the confluence of the Padma and Meghna rivers and adjoining river islands in Munshiganj; the Meghna River near Raipur in Lakshmipur; and the river islands along the Meghna near Hizla and Mehendiganj in Barishal.

Fishermen are injured or killed in these attacks, and their money, belongings and catches are looted. As a result, fishermen, vessel operators and passengers live in fear after dusk.

Shah Alam Mallick said that large-scale day-and-night operations by the Coast Guard, police and fisheries department to protect mother hilsa in the Padma and Meghna rivers have helped prevent major robberies for now. However, once the operations end and fishermen return to fishing, there is a risk of nighttime robberies in remote river-island areas. He said Coast Guard and police patrols must remain intensified to ensure the safety of fishermen and their property. In his view, increasing patrols along river routes bordering district boundaries and in remote river-island areas would help reduce such crimes.

Rivers swallow evidence, leaving murders unsolved

Cargo vessels are also being targeted by robbers. On 10 October last year, criminals looted approximately 6,500 sacks of fertiliser, weighing 317 metric tonnes, from a bulkhead in the Meghna River near Narsingdi. The River Police later arrested 11 people on suspicion of involvement in the incident.

Earlier, on 23 December 2024, seven crew members of the fertiliser-carrying vessel MV Al-Bakhera were hacked and had their throats slit in the Meghna River at Haimechar in Chandpur. The brutal killings aboard the vessel also raised concerns about security along the country's river routes.

Attacks for Refusing to Pay Extortion Money; Police Also Targeted
Ahmadul Kabir Molla, vice-president of the Bangladesh Bulkhead Owners Association, told Prothom Alo that vessels are forced to pay extortion money under the guise of tolls at various locations. He said each vessel is charged Tk 2,000 while loading cargo on the river near Harirampur in Manikganj, Tk 500 at Ilisha in Bhola, and Tk 2,500 at each of Rustampur and Aminbazar in Savar.

He alleged that extortion is being collected from vessels under the pretext of tolls at various points along rivers across the country. He called for administrative intervention to stop the practice.

On the morning of 7 October last year, an organised group armed with traditional weapons, including spears and large machetes, stopped vessels on the Meghna River in Narayanganj and demanded extortion money. When the workers of a bulkhead named MV Zainab Brishti Paribahan refused to pay, two of them, Mohibullah and Zakaria, were beaten and hacked, leaving them injured.

After receiving the news, members of the Chalibhanga River Police Outpost went to the scene to conduct an operation. The extortionists attacked them as well, wielding tridents and spears. Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Maksud and Constables Sohag and Saidur were injured in the attack.
At one point, the police brought the situation under control by firing rubber bullets in self-defence. Two men, Rana and Sazzad, were arrested at the scene.

Mohammad Rezaul Karim, chief of the River Police and Additional Inspector General (Additional IGP), said that difficulties in filing cases and securing witness testimony are hampering efforts to curb extortion. He told Prothom Alo that although people complain about extortion on rivers, no one files cases against the extortionists. When the police file cases themselves, they are unable to prove the offences in court because of a lack of witnesses.

The River Police are also facing attacks while conducting operations to stop illegal sand extraction. On the night of 21 April this year, five members of the Laxmikunda River Police Outpost in Ishwardi, Pabna, were shot while carrying out an operation against illegal sand extraction in the Padma River near the Haripur area of Kushtia Sadar upazila.

In another incident, on the afternoon of 19 August, miscreants stabbed River Police Constable Zakir Hossain and struck him on the head with a brick as he was returning from a river patrol in Kawkhali, Pirojpur. Five police personnel, including River Police Outpost Inspector Mohammad Arman Hossain, were injured while trying to rescue him.

Drugs also being smuggled along waterways

Statistics on cases filed by the River Police include not only drug-related offences but also the transportation of weapons and stolen goods. Mohammad Rezaul Karim, chief of the River Police, said the force would work in coordination with district and metropolitan police to identify the sources of drugs entering the country through river routes and determine how they are being transported.

Rezaul Karim said criminals were being arrested with narcotics during operations along river routes. A database has been compiled using information obtained from those arrested. Individuals involved in various crimes, including snatching and robbery, are also being identified and brought to justice.

Chandpur Records the Highest Number of Cases Over Two Years
Region-wise statistics from the River Police show that Chandpur recorded the highest number of cases in both 2024 and 2025. The region reported 850 cases in 2024, rising to 2,017 the following year. Barishal ranked second in terms of the number of cases in both years, with the figure increasing from 448 to 611.

Among the other regions, the number of cases filed in 2024 was 182 in Chattogram, 120 in Dhaka, 113 in Faridpur, 106 in Narayanganj, 90 in Rajshahi, 58 in Sylhet, 49 in Kishoreganj, 35 in Tangail and 34 in Khulna.
In 2025, the number of cases stood at 147 in Faridpur, 128 in Dhaka, 121 in Rajshahi, 118 in Chattogram, 91 in Narayanganj, 66 in Tangail, 45 in Sylhet, 30 in Kishoreganj and 25 in Khulna.

In other words, alongside Chandpur and Barishal, the number of cases increased in Faridpur, Dhaka, Rajshahi and Tangail. In contrast, the number declined in Narayanganj, Chattogram, Kishoreganj, Khulna and Sylhet.

During the first nine months of this year, the Dhaka region recorded the highest number of cases—86—in five categories: murder, robbery, kidnapping, piracy and unnatural deaths. Narayanganj followed with 82 cases. Barishal and Rajshahi each recorded 70 cases, followed by Faridpur with 57, Tangail with 32, Khulna with 30, Chattogram and Kishoreganj with 25 each, Chandpur with 22, and Sylhet with six cases. However, these figures cannot be directly compared with the total number of cases across all categories recorded in the previous two years.

Alamgir Hossain, superintendent of police for the Narayanganj region, told Prothom Alo that people are being murdered and their bodies dumped in the region’s rivers under the cover of darkness. Bodies dumped in other rivers also drift downstream into rivers in Narayanganj. According to him, other types of crime are not particularly prevalent in the rivers in this area.

Challenges of monitoring vast waterways

According to data from the River Police Headquarters, the country’s navigable waterways extend for 7,500 kilometres during the monsoon season. In the dry season, this length decreases to 4,500 kilometres. Of this, vessels regularly navigate approximately 3,500 kilometres of waterways. Ensuring security across this vast expanse of water presents a major challenge for the River Police.

The chief of the River Police said the force has 124 outposts in areas adjoining the country’s rivers. Personnel stationed at these outposts patrol the waterways and gather information about criminals. Operations based on this intelligence have yielded positive results.

However, Muhammad Umar Faruk, a professor in the Department of Criminology and Police Science at Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University in Tangail, believes that many crimes go unreported and are therefore not reflected in official statistics. He told Prothom Alo that crime along river routes is on the rise and that the actual number of incidents is higher than the figures suggest.

According to the criminologist, the River Police’s role should extend beyond patrolling waterways; surveillance and oversight must also be strengthened to control crime. To achieve this, the force needs to be strengthened by addressing shortages of personnel, equipment and training.

Crime-prone locations must be identified, and coordinated operations should be conducted there in collaboration with other law enforcement agencies to bring criminal gangs to justice. Through such measures, crime along river routes can gradually be reduced.

item.title: TOP SHOTS (24 October 2026)
France protests: Bangladeshi-owned shops also vandalised, looted; business owners anxious
item.description:
Several establishments were extensively vandalised and looted in France last week amid ongoing protests over the rising cost of living. Several businesses owned by expatriate Bangladeshis in Paris were also damaged in the violence.

Fearing further violence, Bangladeshi business owners and other expatriates are now worried about their businesses and personal safety. To bring the situation under control, the French government has announced the deployment of around 70,000 police officers and gendarmerie personnel across the country on Saturday.

During last week's protests, a mobile phone accessories and electronics shop owned by a Bangladeshi expatriate businessman named Hasan in Paris was extensively vandalised and looted. The affected businessman said his shop contained goods worth around €90,000, all of which were looted. As a result, he has suffered significant financial losses.

Bangladeshi expatriates involved in money transfer and currency exchange businesses in various parts of Paris are also deeply concerned. Bangladeshi entrepreneurs operating small outlets of financial service providers such as Ria and MoneyGram fear that their shops could be targeted if violence breaks out on the streets again.

They said such financial transaction outlets have previously been among the businesses most frequently looted during protest movements.

According to information from the Paris city authorities, 451 shops had been vandalised in Paris alone during the violence on 17 and 18 October, as of 21 October. In addition, according to the French government, several thousand businesses across the country have been affected.

Alan Khan Chowdhury, owner of Union Mart in Paris, said business activities had come to a standstill amid the ongoing unrest. The situation has created concerns among business owners about the security of their shops.

He hoped that the situation would return to normal soon and that people would regain a sense of relief in their daily lives.

Alongside business owners, ordinary expatriate workers have also been left facing uncertainty. Monir Hossain, who works in food delivery in Paris, said the disruption caused by the protests had made delivering food extremely difficult and that they constantly feared for their safety.

Meanwhile, the risks have increased further for expatriates who do not have valid legal documents. A daily wage worker in Paris said police checks and increased surveillance in all directions had made it difficult even to leave home for work.

Local business companies in France have taken initiatives to support businesses affected by the violence. The French Federation of Commerce Associations has started collecting information about affected businesses and initiating assistance procedures. The Confederation of French Commerce has also expressed solidarity with affected business owners and employees.

Meanwhile, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Paris and the Île-de-France region is helping affected business owners prepare insurance documents, apply for compensation and receive administrative assistance.

Under the assistance measures announced by the French government, the state will cover the cost of partial unemployment benefits for employees under certain conditions. Other measures include extensions for paying taxes and social contributions, interest-free loans of up to €50,000, and a special fund for eligible small businesses.

Bangladeshi business organisations and community leaders in France need to take coordinated initiatives to ensure that Bangladeshi expatriate entrepreneurs can easily access these legal and financial assistance programmes offered by local authorities.

Although expatriate business owners remain concerned about the possibility of further violence, the overall number of Bangladeshi-owned businesses affected has not yet been officially confirmed.

Students, the labour union CGT and activists of the Yellow Vest movement have been protesting in France over grievances related to the rising cost of living, higher fuel prices and various problems at educational institutions. In the wake of last week's violence, arson and clashes, the authorities have taken maximum precautionary measures ahead of Saturday's protests.

Meanwhile, one person was killed and four others injured in a shooting in the western Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière on Friday. Although counterterrorism authorities are investigating the incident, it has not yet been confirmed whether it has any direct connection with the ongoing protests.

For security reasons, authorities have announced that Paris's world-famous Louvre Museum, Musée d'Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais will remain closed to visitors on Saturday. In addition, local administrations have issued special alerts advising people to exercise caution when travelling through certain areas of Paris and sensitive locations in other cities.

People are advised to exercise caution in Paris areas

Ahead of Saturday's protests, the Paris authorities have taken several precautionary measures. People have been advised to exercise caution when travelling through central Paris, particularly the areas around Bastille, République, Nation and Les Halles.

Those who need to go out for work have been advised to check the latest public transport updates and police instructions before setting out.

People have also been urged to avoid protest hotspots and large gatherings unless absolutely necessary, while foreign nationals living in France have been advised to carry proof of their valid legal documents.

People have also been warned against buying or selling goods looted during the protests. Under French criminal law, purchasing, possessing or selling goods obtained through criminal activities or stolen property is a serious offence. Anyone found guilty of such an offence may face up to five years in prison and a fine of up to €375,000.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,222 as eight die in 24 hours
item.description:
Eight more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Saturday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,222.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all eight of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,118, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the eight new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,014 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Saturday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 219,884.
During the same period, 51 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,324.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 195,514 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 187,605 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Import-export operations resume at Benapole port after eight-day closure
item.description:
Import-export operations have resumed at Benapole land port following an eight-day suspension for the Sharadiya Durga Puja festival.
Passenger movement between Bangladesh and India remained unaffected during the closure, with travellers carrying valid passports continuing to cross the border.
Trade operations resumed at 9am on Saturday. Between 9am and 10am, 35 cargo trucks entered Bangladesh from India, while 11 trucks left Bangladesh for India.
The port typically handles more than 500 truckloads of imports from India and around 200 truckloads of exports to India daily.
Badruzzaman Boni, general secretary of the Benapole C&F Staff Association, said import-export activities had remained suspended for eight days due to public holidays for Durga Puja. Operations resumed on Saturday following the end of the holidays.
Ruhul Amin, acting director of Benapole Port, also confirmed that trade had been suspended during the festival, one of the major religious celebrations of the Hindu community. He said import-export activities had now resumed at the land port.

item.title: Sajek road blockade enters third day; tourism disrupted
item.description:
The indefinite road blockade at Sajek in Rangamati continued for the 3rd day on Saturday with joint forces maintaining patrols to keep the law-and-order situation under control.
The blockade was enforced jointly by Sajek Ganadhikar Rakkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association to press for their three demands, including the immediate removal of armed members of Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (Santu group) from the area and ensuring the security of local residents.
However, there was no report of any untoward incident.
Army, police, and other law enforcement agencies have been working jointly to ensure the safety of people staying in Sajek and maintain peace in the area.
Meanwhile, a half-day road and waterway blockade was observed in Khagrachhari in protest against the gunfight at Ujjobazar in Sajek on Saturday.
Chhatra-Janata Sangram Parishad has announced a half-day road and waterway blockade in Rangamati and Khagrachhari districts from 5am in support of the ongoing movement in Sajek.
Early in the morning, protesters set tyres on fire and blocked a road in South Khobongpuria area of the district town.
Later, members of the law enforcement agencies removed the burning tyres and cleared the road for traffic.
Earlier on Thursday, nearly 3,000 tourists stranded in Sajek Valley were evacuated with the help of the Army and police amid the indefinite road blockade.
Armed UPDF members allegedly opened fire on tourists and members of law enforcement agencies during the evacuation.

item.title: Hefazat ameer opposes Tongi grounds use by Saad supporters
item.description:
Allama Shah Muhibullah Babunagari, ameer of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, has opposed allowing supporters of Maulana Saad Kandhalvi to use the Tongi Bishwa Ijtema grounds for their upcoming Ijtema.
The position was announced at a national consultative meeting held at the Tin-shed Shobjbari point of the Ijtema grounds on Saturday.
The meeting brought together Islamic scholars and senior religious leaders representing all 64 districts.
At a press conference after the meeting, the scholars said the government had contacted Babunagari about allowing supporters of Maulana Saad Kandhalvi to use the grounds for three days. Babunagari had said he would respond after consulting senior Islamic scholars.
Following the consultations, the scholars placed two demands before the government.
First, they called on the government to maintain its previous decision not to allow supporters of Maulana Saad Kandhalvi to use the Tongi Bishwa Ijtema grounds after 2025.
Second, they urged authorities to expedite investigations into murder cases filed over incidents at Tongi in 2018 and 2024 and submit charge sheets. The cases are being investigated by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI).
The scholars also called for prayer gatherings at madrasas, markaz centres and other religious institutions across the country in connection with the Ijtema organized by supporters of Maulana Saad Kandhalvi.
They warned that if pressure were exerted on the government or disorder arose, they would launch programs in districts across the country under the direction of the central leadership in Dhaka.

item.title: Gas supply to remain suspended in parts of Dhaka for four hours
item.description:
Gas supply will remain suspended for four hours in several areas of the capital on Saturday due to emergency repairs to a pipeline leak, Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Ltd has said.
The suspension will remain in effect from 2pm to 6pm on Saturday, affecting all categories of consumers in Nadda, Kalachandpur, Bashundhara, Joar Sahara, Bhatara and Baridhara J Block, as well as adjoining areas along both sides of the road from Notun Bazar to Kuril Bishwa Road.
In a notice, Titas Gas authorities apologised to consumers for the temporary inconvenience caused by the repair work.

item.title: Mia Sattar made chairman of Russia-Bangladesh Business Council
item.description:
Bangladeshi born Russian businessman Mia Sattar has been appointed chairman of the Russia-Bangladesh Business Council.
A well-known entrepreneur in Russian business circles, he heads National Group.
The council’s organizational meeting was held on Thursday at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the Russian Federation in Moscow.
Vladimir Padalko, vice president of the chamber, chaired the meeting. He welcomed and congratulated Sattar on his new role.
Padalko said the council’s work should be based on the real needs of entrepreneurs.
Its main tasks will be preparing analyses of the Bangladesh market for Russian regions, identifying promising areas of cooperation and finding barriers to market entry.
He also stressed the importance of providing individual support to companies interested in working in Bangladesh.
According to Padalko, the council will serve as an aide to the Russia-Bangladesh intergovernmental commission. Specific problems in doing business and implementing joint projects will be raised at the government level by pooling entrepreneurs’ proposals.
Mohammad Nazrul Islam, Bangladesh’s ambassador to Russia, recalled the historic friendship between the two countries. Citing the Soviet Union’s support during Bangladesh’s independence, he said the new platform would boost mutually beneficial cooperation. He added that the embassy was ready to extend all kinds of support to the council’s work.
Vyacheslav Ermolaev, head of the Second Asia Department at Russia’s foreign ministry, said Bangladesh is Russia’s second-largest trading partner in South Asia after India.
He cited the construction of the Rooppur nuclear power plant as one of the key joint projects.
He also pointed to the complexity of financial transactions and the need to widen the list of traded goods.
Anastasia Romanova, head of the South Asia division in the bilateral cooperation department of Russia’s economic development ministry, said the council would allow the intergovernmental commission’s agenda to be broadened in line with business needs. She named energy, chemicals, the agro-industrial sector and information technology as promising areas.
At the meeting, Sattar outlined opportunities for cooperation in energy, agriculture, digital technology, transport infrastructure and light industry. Possible initiatives include building a solar power plant and grain warehouse in Bangladesh, and developing an industrial park in Dhaka on the site of Russia’s former trade representation.
He said Russian companies are already working with Bangladeshi garment factories and importing readymade garments and food products. Work is also under way to secure accreditation for Bangladeshi fish and seafood suppliers to enter the markets of Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union.
The meeting presented the council’s executive directorate and a proposed 2026-27 work plan.
Stanislav Simakov has been appointed executive director.
Interested organizations have been asked to send proposals.
A business meeting of entrepreneurs from the two countries will be prepared in Dhaka on the sidelines of the intergovernmental commission meeting in November.
Also present were Vladimir Polzhkov, general secretary of the Russian Association for International Cooperation; Evgenia Igorova of the SME Corporation; Tatiana Belkevich, president of the Russian Association of Fashion Industry; and Saltanat Sakambayova of NOVATEK.

item.title: Ronan Sullivan included in Bangladesh’s preliminary squad for SAFF Championship
item.description:
Ronan Sullivan has been included in Bangladesh’s 28-member preliminary squad for the SAFF Championship 2026, with the United States-based forward set to get an opportunity to make his senior international debut after impressing for the country’s junior team.
The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) announced the preliminary squad on Saturday for the regional tournament, which will be held in Dhaka from November 5 to 17.
Ronan, who represented Bangladesh in the SAFF U-20 Championship in the Maldives in April, played an important role in the young Bengal Tigers’ title-winning campaign. He scored twice against Pakistan before helping Bangladesh beat India in the final to lift the trophy.
England-based forward Mohammed Mahe Khan has also earned a place in the preliminary squad after represnting Bangladesh at the U-20 level in the AFC U-20 Asian Cup qualifiers in Uzbekistan earlier this year. The 18-year-old plays for English lower-tier club Moulton FC and has impressed this season, scoring nine goals in seven appearances.
The inclusion of the Bangladesh-origin strikers comes as head coach Thomas Dooley looks to strengthen the national team’s attacking options following a difficult campaign in the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup last month.
The preliminary squad also features three overseas-based players who made their Bangladesh senior international debuts during the FIFA ASEAN Cup in September.
England-based winger Farhaan Ali Wahid, Japan-based forward Shuki Itofusa and London-born defender Zidane Alexander Yousuf have all retained their places in the squad.
Farhaan, who is on loan at Boreham Wood from Fulham’s youth setup, made his debut against Malaysia on September 25. Shuki came on as a second-half substitute in the same match, while Zidane also made his first appearance for Bangladesh during the 3-0 defeat in Jakarta.
Bangladesh have been drawn in Group A alongside Bhutan and Sri Lanka, while defending champions India, Pakistan and the Maldives make up Group B. Nepal are absent from the current schedule following their suspension by FIFA.
The hosts will open their campaign against Bhutan at the National Stadium in Dhaka on November 5.
Bangladesh last hosted the SAFF Championship in 2018 and won their only title in 2003.
The home side will be aiming to make the most of home advantage as they seek to end a 23-year wait for another regional crown.
Bangladesh's 28-man squad:
Mitul Marma, Sujon Hossain, Mehdi Hasan Srabon, Topu Barman, Bishwanath Ghosh, Md Saad Uddin, Md Rahmat Mia, Zidane Alexander Yousuf, Md Isa Faysal, Tariq Raihan Kazi, Zayyan Ahmed, Md Sohel Rana, Sohel Rana, Mohammad Ridoy, Hamza Choudhury, Shamit Shome, Syed Quazem Kirmanee Shah, Jamal Bhuiyan, Foysal Ahmed Fahim, Fahamedul Islam, Minhazul Karim Shadin, Mohammed Ibrahim, Shuki Itofusa, Farhaan Ali Wahid, Sheikh Morsalin, Rakib Hossain, Ronan Sullivan, Mohammed Mahe Khan

item.title: Bangladesh hold Wales to goalless draw in FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival opener
item.description:
Bangladesh U-15 national football team began their campaign at the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival 2026 with a goalless draw against Wales at the Hovsan Competition Complex in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Saturday.
Both teams created several scoring opportunities in the Group G encounter but failed to find the breakthrough, with the match ending 0-0.
Bangladesh are in a six-team group alongside Fiji, Burundi, Indonesia, Portugal and Wales. The young Bangladeshi side are scheduled to face Portugal and Indonesia on Sunday before taking on Burundi and Fiji in their remaining group matches on Monday.
The tournament will conclude with the finals on October 30.
The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival features an innovative festival-style format. Matches are played in an eight-a-side format over two 20-minute halves, with rolling substitutions, kick-ins and smaller pitches.
A total of 189 teams are taking part in the event. Among them, 78 teams, including Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and the Maldives from South Asia, have never previously competed at a FIFA World Cup at any age level, in either men's or women's football.

item.title: Neymar backs Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil election
item.description:
Brazilian football star Neymar threw his support behind right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of a tight runoff election against leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday.
The all-time leading goalscorer for Brazil's national team, Neymar openly supported Flavio's father, far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, saying he had "similar values" to his own.
He had not commented on this year's campaign, but appeared in an Instagram video with pro-Bolsonaro lawmaker Nikolas Ferreira on Friday.
"What was Neymar's jersey number at Barcelona? It was eleven. And what do eleven plus eleven add up to?" asked Ferreira, turning the camera to show Neymar using his fingers to form the number 22 -- the number assigned to Flavio on the ballot.
"It's not about politics, it's just football here," added Ferreira, one of the most prominent figures on the Brazilian right in Congress, with a wink.
Neymar retired from international football in July after Brazil's World Cup defeat by Norway, and is playing for Brazilian club Santos.
Polls show Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro in a statistical dead heat ahead of Sunday's vote.

item.title: Mourinho must stop Barca as Clasico tensions resume
item.description:
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho will renew one of football's most bitter rivalries on Sunday when he takes charge of his first Clasico since returning to the club, with La Liga leaders Barcelona awaiting him at Camp Nou.
The Portuguese veteran's first spell at Madrid was defined in large part by his battle to end Barca's dominance under Pep Guardiola, with relations between the Spanish giants slumping to their lowest ebb.
Mourinho managed to break Barca's spell by guiding Real Madrid to the Spanish title in 2012, the crowning achievement of his reign from 2010-13.
Clasicos became increasingly compelling during that period, some would say not for the right reasons, as he and his staff clashed with their Barcelona counterparts both pitch-side and verbally in the media.
The 63-year-old worked as an assistant at Barca under Bobby Robson and Louis van Gaal in the 1990s but was overlooked for Guardiola in 2008 when the Catalans replaced Frank Rijkaard.
Mourinho's frequent battles with Guardiola, Lionel Messi and even with Madrid's own icons like Iker Casillas sometimes overshadowed his sporting achievements.
The most infamous flashpoint was when Mourinho poked then Barca assistant coach Tito Vilanova in the eye in August 2011.
Earlier that year, at the end of the prior season, Madrid and Barca clashed four times in just 18 days, illustrating the intensity of the rivalry.
The first was in La Liga, a 1-1 draw, which helped Barcelona take a step towards retaining the Spanish title as Madrid trailed them.
Mourinho's Madrid beat Barca to win the Copa del Rey in the second, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring the winner in extra-time.
Then the Catalans got the better of Los Blancos in a Champions League semi-final double header, winning the first leg 2-0 in the Santiago Bernabeu, with Madrid defender Pepe sent off. Mourinho called it a "scandal".
Barcelona held Real Madrid to a 1-1 draw in the second leg to reach the final, which they went on to win.
It was in this period that Guardiola said he could not and would not compete with the "boss" Mourinho in the press room.
- Stopping Flick's Barca -
Mourinho has hit the ground running in his second spell at Madrid in that regard.
The coach brandished print-outs of incidents after losing the derby clash to try and prove his point that Atletico Madrid deserved two red cards, and refused to attend a press conference after Vinicius Junior was sent off against Villarreal.
Many believe Mourinho employs these tactics as a distraction to take the pressure off his team when they are not performing.
A victory in the Clasico might encourage him to focus on the football, and stopping Hansi Flick's side -- back-to-back Spanish champions -- is one of the main reasons he was rehired by president Florentino Perez.
Flick's Barca have won six of seven Clasicos against Real Madrid since the German arrived, scoring 22 goals and shipping only 11.
Mourinho insists it is impossible for his team to be at the level he wants them to be at after such a short time in charge.
"I've been here for over a hundred days. Obviously, we are not where I want, but there are things we are doing better today than before," said the coach.
Madrid have won their last four matches between La Liga and the Champions League, and after sharing minutes around early in the season, some preferences are emerging.
Although Mourinho said initially he did not see midfielder Federico Valverde as a right-back, where he has been used in the past, he has selected the Uruguayan there in the last two games, ahead of Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold.
"We created a lot on that side, and Fede had a fantastic match," said Mourinho after the Leipzig win.
In Valverde's place in midfield Mourinho deployed Arda Guler against Sevilla on Sunday and then Bernardo Silva against the German side, with Madrid improving on the ball and retaining more possession.
However the Clasico poses a different challenge. Mourinho, who deployed defender Pepe in midfield against Barca, may revert to type to try and spoil the hosts' flowing football.

item.title: Shuki on target as Fortis end AFC Challenge League campaign with win
item.description:
Fortis FC ended their debut AFC Challenge League campaign on a high, coming from behind to beat Tajikistan’s FC Regar-TadAZ 3-1 in Group C on Friday for their first victory in the competition.
Both sides finished their campaigns with three points, but Fortis secured second place in the four-team group on goal difference, behind Kuwait’s Qadsia SC. The Bangladesh Football League outfit had lost their opening match 3-0 to Qadsia before suffering a 2-1 defeat to FC Goa.
Regar-TadAZ took the lead in the 12th minute when Ndongo Foe’s clever flick sent Sherzod Makhamadiev through on the right. The No. 10 cut inside Monir Alam before firing past Sujan Perera.
However, the match took a decisive turn five minutes later when Regar-TadAZ goalkeeper Severin Takam was sent off for tripping Noriki Akada outside the box after the Japanese forward intercepted Martin Ako Assomo’s underhit back pass.
Replacement goalkeeper Shakhobiddin Makhmudzoda immediately had to make a save, keeping out Pa Omar’s curling free-kick.
Fortis pressed forward with their numerical advantage but missed a golden opportunity to equalise in the 35th minute. Omar chested the ball down for Akada inside the box, but the Japanese forward blazed his effort over the bar.
Regar-TadAZ head coach Alisher Tukhtaev opted against instructing his side to sit deep and defend their lead, leaving the contest open after the break.
Fortis took full advantage, drawing level in the 67th minute. Makhmudzoda dived to stop second-half substitute Shuki Itofusa but could only divert the ball into Omar’s path. The forward then picked out Rafayel Tudu at the far post, where he finished with a backheel.
Fortis completed the turnaround just four minutes later. Ananta Tamang headed Mohammad Ibrahim’s cross into the path of Shian Kawasaki, who unleashed a volley past Makhmudzoda to put the Bangladesh side ahead.
Mohammad Masud’s men sealed the victory in the 88th minute, with Omar setting up Shuki for a composed, curling side-footed finish.
Shuki, the Japanese-Bangladeshi forward who made his international debut for Bangladesh during the FIFA ASEAN Cup in September, came off the bench in the 64th minute and made an immediate impact with a goal to cap a memorable end to Fortis’s maiden continental campaign.

item.title: Is social media quietly ruining your relationship?
item.description:
Many people are comparing their own relationships with the romantic videos, intimate moments, and expensive gifts they see on social media. Content like this creates expectations of extra attention from a partner, special arrangements, and cinematic romantic gestures. When those expectations go unmet, disappointment, sulking, and friction can follow.
According to a report by the Indian outlet India Today, relationship-themed reels circulating on social media are shaping modern love and dating. These videos offer easy solutions to relationship problems in a very short time. But real-life relationships are not always so simple.
A recent survey by the Indian dating app QuackQuack gathered the views of more than 10,000 people aged 22 to 38. Participants included people dating in both big cities and smaller towns. The survey found that many people begin to reassess their own relationships after seeing relationship advice on social media. Yet advice given in a single video may not apply equally to every relationship.
On social media, you often see statements such as “If your partner truly loves you, they’ll do everything on their own,” or “What’s the point of a relationship if you don’t get princess treatment?”
After watching such videos, some people expect the same behavior from their partners. When those expectations aren’t met, sulking or arguments begin.
The survey analyzed responses from 4,694 participants over the age of 25. Many of them feel that problems arise when the same set of relationship rules is applied to every couple.
For example, if someone wants to spend some time alone after work, that is not always a sign of emotional distance. In the survey, 60% of the men disagreed with that notion. Meanwhile, 38% of participants said that a partner who cannot arrange a grand date should not automatically be considered less caring.
Ravi Mittal, founder and CEO of the dating app QuackQuack, said that real-life circumstances and mutual understanding matter in a relationship.
He said it is not right to apply every piece of advice found on social media blindly to one’s own relationship. Not calling someone can sometimes be a sign of neglect, but it isn’t in every case.
However, the survey participants do not call the influence of social media entirely negative. Forty-eight percent of participants believe the influence of social media on relationships cannot be completely denied.
About 27% of women in their thirties said that this kind of content sometimes helps them understand certain aspects of relationships in a new way. In the survey, four out of every ten people said they had learned about personal boundaries, or about their own needs in a relationship, by watching other people’s relationship content.
Many of the relationship moments seen on social media are deliberately staged. Multiple takes, special arrangements, and carefully selected photos go into creating a picture-perfect romantic scene. Viewers know these are not the full picture of any relationship. Even so, many people compare their own relationships with those moments.
In the survey, 3,347 participants said they understand that only selected moments of relationships are shown online, yet they still compare their own relationships to them.
Akriti from Bengaluru, a survey participant, said that trends on social media such as lavish marriage proposals, surprise gifts, and dreamlike couple photos can make an ordinary relationship feel like a failure.
Taking inspiration from others is fine, she said, but when it turns into comparison, even the small expressions of love in a relationship lose their value.
Before expecting the same behavior from a partner after seeing someone else’s romance on social media, it is important to understand your own needs. Does the relationship need more time, clearer communication, or reassurance?
You can try to work that out through open conversation with your partner. After all, it is not the staged moments of other people’s relationships but mutual understanding and real needs that help a relationship move forward.

item.title: Japanese author Ryu Murakami dies at 74
item.description:
Japanese novelist and filmmaker Ryu Murakami, known for his explorations of violence, alienation, and the darker sides of society, has died at the age of 74.
Murakami died at his home on October 17, according to his Japanese publisher, Gentosha.
Often described as the enfant terrible of contemporary Japanese literature, Murakami wrote more than 40 novels and short story collections. His works combined dark humour, graphic violence, drug use and sexuality with criticism of Japanese and American society.
Born in 1952 in Sasebo, Nagasaki prefecture, Murakami was the son of two teachers. During high school, he played drums in a rock band and was placed under house arrest for three months after participating in a rooftop protest.
He published his debut novel, Almost Transparent Blue , in 1976 while still a student. Narrated by a character named Ryū, the novel portrays the hedonistic lives of disillusioned young people. It won the Gunzo Prize for New Writers and the Akutagawa Prize, one of Japan’s most prestigious literary awards.
Murakami was not related to fellow Japanese novelist Haruki Murakami. Journalist David Pilling described Ryu Murakami’s writing as “edgier and angrier” in 2013, comparing Haruki to the Beatles and Ryu to the Rolling Stones.
His other notable works include Coin Locker Babies , In the Miso Soup , Audition , Piercing and Popular Hits of the Showa Era . Many of his books remain unavailable in English translation.
Several of his works have been adapted for film, including Audition , the 1999 horror film directed by Takashi Miike. The story follows a widower who stages fake film auditions to find a new girlfriend.
Writing about the novel in The Guardian in 2009, Scottish author Irvine Welsh praised its prose for its emotional depth and visceral intensity.
Murakami’s third novel, Coin Locker Babies , tells the story of children abandoned in storage lockers and won the Noma Literary New Face Prize. The novel explores the darker aspects of society through a surreal narrative involving alienation, fame, insanity and murder.
Adam Freudenheim, publisher and managing director of Pushkin Press, which publishes Murakami’s translated works in the United Kingdom alongside Bloomsbury, expressed sadness over the author’s death.
He said it had been a privilege to introduce Murakami’s original and cinematic novels to English-speaking readers, adding that the publisher extended its sympathies to the author’s readers worldwide.
